title: Keep exact colours on your board
summary: Add colour cards with a name and HEX value, and line up a palette beside your pictures.
benefit: Keep the colours you've chosen next to the pictures and notes they belong with.
outcome: A colour card called Forest shows its colour and #2F5D50, ready to sit beside your other references.

sections.title: How colour cards work
paragraphs: A colour card is a block of one colour with its name and HEX value underneath. The colour is exactly what you chose: switching DoggyNote between light and dark doesn't change it.
For example, pick fabric colours for a new dog bed: Pumpkin, Brick and Mustard next to a photo of the throw you love, and a Forest green to try against them.

figures.alt: A photo of autumn leaves captioned Autumn leaves throw, followed by four colour cards: Pumpkin #D9822B, Brick #B5442A, Mustard #E2B33C and Forest #2F5D50.
figures.caption: A small palette lined up beside the photo it came from.

flow.entry: Open the board where you're collecting colours. In the tools on the left, Colour is under More.

steps.action: Choose Colour, or drag it to the spot you want. On a phone, tap + at the bottom of the screen, then Colour.
steps.result: A new colour card appears with its colour panel open beside it.

steps.action: Pick a colour from the dots, or type #2F5D50 in the HEX field.
steps.result: The card changes as you go. The last dot, +, opens your device's colour picker for any other colour.

steps.action: Type Forest in the name field (it says “Name this shade…” while it's empty).
steps.result: The name appears on the card above the HEX value.

steps.action: Press Enter, or click anywhere on the board.
steps.result: The panel closes and the card keeps its colour and name.

flow.completion: The card saves as you type and syncs to everyone on the board.
flow.correction: Double-click the card to open its panel again and change it. Undo after closing the panel puts back the colour and name from before you opened it. A HEX value that isn't complete yet doesn't change the card: it keeps the last valid colour.

figures.alt: The Forest colour card, selected, with its panel open underneath: two rows of colour dots with dark green picked, a + for a custom colour, a HEX field showing #2F5D50 and a name field showing Forest.
figures.caption: The colour panel opens right beside the card. Double-click a colour card to open it again.

sections.title: Arrange, copy and find colours
paragraphs: Drag a colour card like any other card, resize it from its corner, or drop it into a column with the rest of a palette. To try a variation without losing the original, right-click the card and choose Duplicate, or press ⌘D (Ctrl+D on Windows).
Fetch finds colour cards by name or HEX value, so typing Forest or 2F5D50 takes you back to the card.

sections.title: Good to know
paragraphs: HEX values can be typed with or without the #, and three-digit values such as #FA0 are expanded to six digits.
People with view-only access can see colour cards and read their values, but can't change them. Colour cards don't take a card tint: the colour is the card.
